Donna di 42 anni con obesità grave e dia: 42-year-old woman with severe obesity and diabetes, positive swab for SARS-CoV-2. Admitted after 3 days of cough, dyspnea, nausea and diarrhea. Descrivi il quadro polmonare e come camb: Describe the lung findings and how they change across the three examinations, then check the devices on the last radiograph.
La polmonite da SARS-CoV-2 in radiografi:
On radiographs, SARS-CoV-2 pneumonia gives bilateral patchy ground-glass opacities and consolidations, predominantly in the middle and lower zones and in the periphery; in the first days the radiograph may be almost normal. Rapid progression to diffuse, confluent opacities indicates diffuse alveolar damage (ARDS) and often precedes intubation. Simple scores (for example RALE or Brixia) describe the extent and help compare examinations.
Bedside radiographs are AP: the heart and mediastinum look wider, the bases are veiled by soft tissue (here severe obesity) and effusions are less visible, because fluid layers posteriorly.
After every procedure the first thing to check is the devices: endotracheal tube (tip about 3-5 cm above the carina), nasogastric or orogastric tube (tip in the stomach, never in the airways), central venous catheter (tip at the junction of the superior vena cava and the right atrium), then pneumothorax and position of the electrodes. When the carina is poorly seen, as here, the report should say so and, if needed, ask for another image.
Radiografia a letto dopo una procedura:: Bedside radiograph after a procedure: first the devices (tube, gastric tube, catheter), then the lungs.
Terapia intensiva e ventilazione invasiv: Intensive care and invasive ventilation for 2 days; discharged after 9 days in hospital (clinical data of the COVID-19-NY-SBU collection).

Le tre immagini sono AP (scritta PORTABL: The three images are AP (PORTABLE label). The cardiothoracic ratio on AP cannot be compared with PA values; the bases are also veiled by soft tissue.

Tubo endotracheale in trachea: verificar: Endotracheal tube in the trachea: check that the tip lies about 3-5 cm above the carina (with the neck in neutral position)
Sondino orogastrico: il percorso va segu: Orogastric tube: follow its course along the esophagus to below the diaphragm; the tip must lie in the stomach
Il sondino (annotato OGT sull'immagine): The tube (labelled OGT on the image) runs down the midline next to the endotracheal tube. A tube in the airways or with its tip in the esophagus is an error to report immediately.
Catetere venoso centrale da destra (giug: Central venous catheter from the right (internal jugular vein), running down towards the superior vena cava: the ideal tip position is at the junction with the right atrium
Tubo endotracheale nel bronco principale: Endotracheal tube in the right main bronchus, with collapse of the left lung
Il tubo è sulla linea mediana e il polmo: The tube is on the midline and the left lung is still aerated in the upper zones.

Giorno 0: opacità bilaterali a chiazze,: Day 0: bilateral patchy opacities, more evident in the middle and lower zones on both sides; apices relatively spared. This is the typical distribution of SARS-CoV-2 pneumonia (bilateral, peripheral and basal).
Giorno 3, mattina: opacità diffuse bilat: Day 3, morning: diffuse bilateral opacities, more extensive than on admission. Day 3, evening: extensive consolidation, especially on the left and at the bases.
RX della sera del giorno 3: il tubo endo: Evening X-ray of day 3: the endotracheal tube runs down the midline in the trachea. With the dense mediastinum and poor penetration the carina is poorly seen: if the tip is not clearly above the carina, a check should be requested.
RX della sera del giorno 3: il catetere: Evening X-ray of day 3: the catheter enters from the right side of the neck and runs down to the right of the trachea. After every catheter, also look for pneumothorax and malposition.
